s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions on the face, chest, abdomen, and limbs
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
key_facts: The patient is a child weighing 30 kg
The patient has no comorbidities or allergies
The patient is not taking any long-term medications
The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions on the face, chest, abdomen, and limbs
The patient reported frequent contact with stray cats
Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 47 mm/h
C-reactive protein is 25.8 mg/L
White blood cell count is 15,390/uL
Eosinophils are 11%
IgE level is 7200 μg/L

shortlist.label: Trichophyton infection
shortlist.why_kept: Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes

shortlist.label: Dermatophytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and positive mycological culture

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions

shortlist.label: Cat scratch disease
shortlist.why_kept: Frequent contact with stray cats and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Sporotrichosis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and potential exposure to infectious agents

raw.rationale: The presence of erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and the mycological culture yielding growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes strongly support this diagnosis, as Trichophyton is a common cause of dermatophytosis.

rejected.label: Trichophyton infection
rejected.why: While Trichophyton infection is a correct identification of the causative agent, dermatophytosis is a more specific diagnosis that encompasses the clinical presentation and the type of infection.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme typically presents with target lesions and is often associated with viral infections or medications, which does not match this patient's presentation or history.

rejected.label: Cat scratch disease
rejected.why: Cat scratch disease is caused by Bartonella henselae and typically presents with lymphadenopathy and a history of a cat scratch, which is not the primary presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Sporotrichosis
rejected.why: Sporotrichosis is caused by Sporothrix schenckii and typically presents with lesions following a lymphocutaneous pattern, which does not match the patient's presentation of widespread skin lesions without a clear lymphocutaneous pattern.
